test_title: PYST 35: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Privatisation can be partial, involving minority shareholding by the private sector. What is the government's shareholding threshold in a PSU for it to be considered privatised?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Less than 51%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) is considered privatised when the government’s shareholding falls **below 51%.**
 
• This threshold ensures that the private sector holds a majority share, providing control and decision-making power.
 
• Privatisation can be partial or complete, depending on the percentage of shares divested by the government.
 
• Privatisation aims to improve efficiency, promote competition, and reduce the financial burden of PSUs on the government.
 
• Examples of privatised PSUs include Air India and Bharat Aluminium Company Limited (BALCO).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privatisation**

 
 
• It refers to the transfer of ownership, management, or control of a government-owned enterprise to the private sector.
 
• It can occur through mechanisms like disinvestment, public-private partnerships, or outright sale of assets.
 
• Privatisation is often undertaken to enhance efficiency and reduce government expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment**
 
 
• Disinvestment involves the sale or liquidation of government-owned shares in PSUs.
 
• It is aimed at raising revenue and encouraging private sector participation.
 
• Major disinvestment initiatives include Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and IDBI Bank.
 
 
 
• **Types of Privatisation**
 
 
• **Partial Privatisation:** Government retains a minority shareholding (more than 49%) while transferring control to the private sector.
 
• **Complete Privatisation:** Government sells 100% of its stake to the private sector, relinquishing all ownership rights.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Privatisation**
 
 
• Improves operational efficiency due to private sector expertise.
 
• Promotes competition and innovation in industries.
 
• Reduces fiscal burden on the government.
 
• Enhances service quality for consumers.
